messages:
anya: noticed a small spike in inter-region handshakes failing after last night's cert rotation, throwing TLS_ALERT_UNKNOWN_CA for some east->eu paths
matt: ugh, saw some errors in the proxy metrics too, 503 + tls handshake failures around 02:05 UTC
rui: do we have rotator logs? last deploy applied new intermediate chain + updated TLS profile (min TLS 1.3)
rotator-bot: rotator v2.14 completed rotation at 2026-03-20T02:01:18Z, changes: intermediate chain swap, ocsp stapling enabled, sni-strict=true
anya: right — quick check: some older edge proxies still had cached intermediate A and expect chain A. New chain B is valid but intermediate ordering differs. that can break some clients esp if client doesn't re-fetch intermediates
matt: can you paste the exact error from the proxy log?
anya: log snippet: 
```
proxy[proxy-2] 2026-03-20T02:06:12Z WARN tls: handshake failed: remote error: tls: unknown certificate authority (chain verification failed: missing intermediate)
```

carla: this smells like keystore rotation + keystore role change race. I remember we rolled back the keystore-reader role to a narrower policy last week (RBAC change: service account cert-reader lost get/list on secret-keystore in eu).
ops-oncall: confirmed — IAM change PR #487 removed list on secrets for cert-rotator-sa in eu for compliance constraints. It was applied 02:00 UTC.
rui: timeline matches: RBAC change at 02:00, rotator ran 02:01, proxies started pulling new cert chain but couldn't read some cached intermediates from secret store -> partial chain published
matt: so two issues: 1) rotator published chain B but some proxies couldn't retrieve the full bundle due to RBAC, 2) some clients still trust chain A ordering and don't accept B ordering.
anya: mitigation options: a) regrant read/list to cert-rotator-sa in eu and re-run rotator to ensure full bundle is published, b) roll back to previous chain A on rotator while we investigate, c) temporarily relax sni-strict on proxies to allow accepting presented chain if top cert validates to root.
carla: +1 on regranting read, that's lowest blast radius. we should also enable audit logging for the secret access in eu so we can show the denied calls.
ops-oncall: I can re-add the list permission for cert-rotator-sa now, will do a canary in eu-west-1 group. doing it in 2 mins.
rotator-bot: NOTE: rotator run is idempotent but will only publish what it can read locally. ensure keystore perms first.
matt: after perms are back, we should run:
```
kubectl -n cert-ops exec deploy/rotator -- /bin/rotator --publish --target-region=eu-west-1
```
and watch rotator logs for any KMS decrypt errors.
anya: also check KMS audit log for Decrypt failures — if the secret exists but KMS decrypt fails due to key policy or IAM principal, that will also produce partial bundles.
carla: from a compliance view, we need to record the RBAC change and the subsequent correction in the audit trail. open a ticket and attach S3/cw logs.
ops-oncall: perms restored at 02:12 UTC, rotator re-run started at 02:14 UTC. initial logs show full bundle upload successful by 02:16 UTC.
rui: still seeing a small fraction of inbound handshakes failing from a handful of edge proxies that never refreshed chain (TTL/caching). we should invalidate prefix cache and trigger rolling restart of the proxy pods on those nodes.
matt: steps for rolling restart (canary first):
1) label eu proxies: kubectl -n proxy-scale get pods -l region=eu -o name | head -n 3
2) kubectl rollout restart deployment/proxy-eu --selector=region=eu --grace-period=30 --timeout=5m
3) observe handshake metrics and success ratio

anya: after restart handshake success jumped back to 99.98% for the canary pods. full rollout in progress.
carla: follow-ups: 
- revert the RBAC PR that tightened secrets read until we have an audited plan for rotator access (or create a narrower role that allows read/list only for the rotator service account and only on cert/* secrets)
- add an alert on certbundle_mismatch_rate > 0.1% per-region
- add a post-rotation verification job that validates chain ordering across a sample of proxies in each region

ops-oncall: created ticket SEC-1429 for the role rollback + new scoped role, assigned to carla. added logs to the ticket (cloudtrail entries and rotator logs).
rui: couple questions for the design doc: 
- KMS: should rotator decrypt using a cross-region key or use per-region keys? cross-region key caused some latency and policy complexity during last KMS policy tighten.
- Audit logs: we need a clear schema for rotated artifacts (bundle_id, published_at, regions, rotator_commit, keystore_version) to store in S3 + index in the audit DB.

carla: answers: 
- prefer per-region KMS keys with controlled IAM trust (simpler and lower blast radius). if cross-region keys are critical, document the fallback and require explicit approval.
- agree on the audit schema, I'll draft a minimal JSON schema and add to SEC-1429.

anya: tiny nit — TLS config hardening: sni-strict made sense for security but it's a migration risk. we should gate sni-strict behind a post-rotation verification and a rollout window (default off, opt-in per-region) until all proxies pass chain verification.
matt: also add a periodic job to validate certificate path building from random client environments (mobile, java8, older openssl) to catch ordering/trust oddities earlier.
ops-oncall: full rollout completed 02:45 UTC, metrics back to baseline. closing the incident, creating postmortem notes in the incident channel.
carla: thanks everyone. I'll follow up with the scoped RBAC role, audit schema, and a proposed preflight checklist for future rotations. :thumbsup:
